findings.title: Duplicate method definition `downsize` silently overrides first
findings.body: Two `def self.downsize` methods are defined with different signatures (one taking max_width, max_height, the other taking dimensions). Ruby allows redefinition, so the second definition (`downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`) silently overwrites the first. Any existing caller using `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` (two numeric args) will now break because the new method only accepts a single `dimensions` string argument, causing an ArgumentError or wrong behavior at runtime.

findings.title: Repeated downsizing can degrade image quality without guarantee of success
findings.body: The loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` up to 5 times, each time overwriting the file with a lossy re-encode of the previous resize output. This compounds quality loss unnecessarily, and if `max_image_size_kb` is set very low or the image can't be reduced further (e.g. already minimal size), the loop just exhausts attempts without any error reporting to the user — the oversized file is still uploaded afterward silently exceeding the configured limit.

findings.title: Download size limit changed from configurable setting to hardcoded value
findings.body: `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` replaces the previous `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` limit with a hardcoded 10MB. This decouples the enforced download size cap from the site's configured max_image_size_kb setting, meaning admins can no longer control the API download size limit via settings.

findings.title: File size validation hardcoded instead of using site setting
findings.body: `maxSizeKB` is now hardcoded to `10 * 1024` instead of reading `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. This breaks the configurability of max upload size per type (image vs attachment) and is inconsistent with the backend which still uses `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, causing client-side validation to diverge from server-side limits.

findings.title: Error message hardcodes max size instead of using site setting
findings.body: `maxSizeKB` in the 413 error handler is hardcoded to `10 * 1024` rather than `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`, so the error message shown to users may not reflect the actual configured limit.
